2. Mycophenolate, hydroxychloroquine and losartan unchanged.
3. Return in 6 months.

documents.title: Emergency department provider note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — PROVIDER NOTE
Arrival: 03/12/2026 18:05, brought in by friends.

HPI: 34 year old woman brought in for strange behavior after spending the day at an outdoor music festival. Friends say she was dancing wildly, kept saying she was overheating, and drank very little water. History is limited by agitation; obtained from friends and, later, the patient. Medications include sertraline and sumatriptan, and she takes an over-the-counter dextromethorphan cough syrup now and then for a long-standing throat irritation. She has lupus and is on immunosuppressive therapy. Friends deny alcohol or drugs at the festival; patient later confirms.

PMH: anxiety/OCD, migraine, asthma, SLE with kidney involvement.
Home medications (from our system): albuterol HFA as needed; fluticasone HFA 44 mcg 2 puffs twice daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: seasonal pollens; no known drug allergies.

Exam: T 39.7 C (103.5 F), HR 120, BP 168/94, RR 24, SpO2 97% RA.
Awake, agitated, intermittently combative. Pupils dilated. Profuse sweating. Bowel sounds increased. Neuro: inducible clonus at both ankles, hyperreflexia in both lower extremities, mild rigidity. Neck supple. No photophobia. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. No rash.
Fingerstick glucose normal.

MDM: Clinical picture of serotonin toxicity (clonus, hyperreflexia, hyperthermia, agitation, mydriasis, diaphoresis) in a patient on sertraline and sumatriptan with dextromethorphan use, plus heat and dehydration. Because she is immunosuppressed and febrile, infection was evaluated as well: CBC, CMP, CK, urinalysis, blood and urine cultures and chest x-ray.

Results: CBC normal. CMP normal, creatinine 0.9. CK normal. Urinalysis bland. Chest x-ray clear. Cultures pending.

Treatment: active external cooling, IV fluids, IV benzodiazepine for agitation, cyproheptadine by mouth (loading dose, then scheduled). Sertraline and sumatriptan held. Dextromethorphan stopped.

Course: by 22:00 temperature 37.6, HR 94, calmer, clonus diminishing.

Diagnosis: serotonin syndrome.
Disposition: ED observation overnight.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: ED observation discharge
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED OBSERVATION — DISCHARGE NOTE
Observation 03/12/2026 to 03/13/2026

Diagnosis: serotonin syndrome.

Course: cooled, IV fluids, benzodiazepine and cyproheptadine. Temperature normal since midnight. Agitation resolved; alert and oriented, appropriate. Clonus resolved on morning exam; reflexes normal. Tolerating food and fluids. 10:30 vitals: T 36.8, HR 76, BP 120/76, RR 16, SpO2 99%.
Blood and urine cultures no growth so far; final results to PCP.

Instructions:
- Do NOT take dextromethorphan (in many cough and cold products).
- Hold sertraline and sumatriptan until reviewed by your PCP and psychiatrist.
- Hydrate, rest, avoid heat today.
- Follow up with PCP within 1 week.
- Return for fever, confusion, muscle stiffness or twitching.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: ED follow-up — serotonin syndrome
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED FOLLOW-UP

Seen in the ED 3/12 with serotonin syndrome after a day at an outdoor music festival: hyperthermic, agitated, clonus. On sertraline 100 and using sumatriptan, plus an OTC dextromethorphan cough syrup now and then. Cooled, fluids, benzodiazepine, cyproheptadine, observed overnight, home 3/13.

Today: back to normal. No fever, no muscle twitching or stiffness, thinking clearly, sleeping well. Has not taken sertraline, sumatriptan or any cough syrup since. One mild headache, rode it out. Psychiatry has her scheduled next week. The cough syrup was for a scratchy throat she's had for a long time.
Lupus meds taken throughout.

Results: ED CBC, CMP (creatinine 0.9), CK, UA normal; chest x-ray clear; urine culture no growth; blood cultures final no growth at 5 days.

Meds now: prednisone 5 mg daily; mycophenolate 1000 mg BID; hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily; losartan 25 mg daily; fluticasone HFA 44 2 puffs BID; albuterol PRN. Sertraline and sumatriptan on hold. ED list was outdated; ours reconciled.
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (photosensitivity); seasonal tree and grass pollens. Adding dextromethorphan today.

BP 124/78, HR 74, RR 14, T 36.7, SpO2 99%. Wt 66.2 kg.
Calm, alert, oriented, normal affect. Pupils equal and normal size, reactive. No tremor. Tone normal. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric, no clonus at the ankles. Strength and gait normal. Skin dry. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
1. Serotonin syndrome, resolved.
 - Dextromethorphan added to allergy list (serotonin syndrome with sertraline and sumatriptan). Avoid every product that contains it; went through label reading together ("DM", "cough", "nighttime" cold formulas).
 - Sumatriptan OK to use again as needed: no more than a few days a month, and never together with dextromethorphan or other serotonergic OTC products.
 - Sertraline: leaving the restart and dose to psychiatry (appt 3/24). Sent them this note.
2. Throat irritation — long-standing, the reason for the cough syrup. Noted.
3. SLE with lupus nephritis — stable on current regimen.
RTC as planned in summer; sooner as needed.

documents.title: After Visit Summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
What happened: your symptoms in the ED were serotonin syndrome, from too much serotonin activity. The combination of sertraline, sumatriptan and dextromethorphan (the cough syrup) can cause it, and heat and dehydration made it worse.

From now on:
- Never take dextromethorphan. Check labels for "dextromethorphan" or "DM". Many cough, cold and "nighttime" products contain it. It is now on your allergy list.
- Sumatriptan is OK again for migraines, but only a few days a month, and never with cough/cold products like these.
- Sertraline: psychiatry will restart it at your appointment on 3/24. Don't restart it on your own.
- Keep taking all your lupus medicines.

Call us any time with questions about an over-the-counter product before you take it.

OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY — FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 03/24/2026

34 year old woman with GAD and OCD, on sertraline 100 mg daily until 3/12/2026, when she was treated in the ED for serotonin syndrome in the setting of sertraline, sumatriptan and over-the-counter dextromethorphan, plus heat exposure. Sertraline has been held since. Her PCP has put dextromethorphan on her allergy list and allowed limited sumatriptan.

Off sertraline for 12 days. Physically recovered. No compulsions. No suicidal ideation. She would like to resume treatment.
Allergies: dextromethorphan (serotonin syndrome); hydrochlorothiazide (photosensitivity); seasonal pollens.

Mental status: cooperative, mildly anxious, logical, no suicidal ideation.

Plan:
1. Restart sertraline at 50 mg daily.
2. Reviewed warning signs of serotonin toxicity; no dextromethorphan; sumatriptan sparingly as her PCP advised.
3. Return in about 8 weeks to consider returning to 100 mg.

Psychiatry

documents.title: Allergy pill question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Pollen season is back and I'm sneezing nonstop. Is my usual plain antihistamine still ok? I'm paranoid now after the ER. The store also has a 'cold and allergy' version, is that the same?

documents.title: RE: Allergy pill question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your usual plain antihistamine tablet is fine. Skip the "cold and allergy" and any "DM" or cough versions: combination products often add dextromethorphan or decongestants. If the box lists more than one active ingredient, send me a photo before you buy it. Good instinct to ask.

2. Continue to avoid dextromethorphan and other serotonergic over-the-counter products.
